A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same relative-KL generative-model comparison study. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated theorems, figures and tables.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original simulations, coverage and power estimates, and model-comparison confidence intervals on image and text datasets.

after.justification: The original empirical studies are retained, with additional SLQ approximation results, encoder-error sensitivity results and WikiText-2 confidence-interval comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces an optional stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ) procedure for approximating Jacobian log determinants. The relative-KL estimator, conditional extension and CLT/Edgeworth interval procedures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that existing benchmarks switched to SLQ.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same simulated distribution families and transformations, CIFAR-10, CelebA, WikiText-2 and TriviaQA. The added computational and sensitivity checks reuse existing coverage. CelebA was already evaluated in v3 Appendix D.3.

E2.justification: The model-comparison baselines remain kNN KL and Wasserstein estimators with Subsampling/Adaptive HulC, MMD, KSD and relative KID. The compared generative models are retained. SLQ is evaluated as an internal computational approximation rather than another generative-model-comparison baseline.

E3.justification: New checks use the first CIFAR-10 test image with one random probe and 10 Lanczos steps, an encoder-perturbation grid from 0 to 0.05, and varying WikiText-2 sample sizes. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; TriviaQA answer handling is newly disclosed.

E4.justification: Adds an SLQ accuracy check in C.2, encoder-error sensitivity measuring coverage and bias in D.2/Table 4, and a GPT2 versus GPT2-Large sample-size analysis in D.3/Figure 24. Earlier distributional and transformation analyses remain available after relocation.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 newly reports 50 SLQ runs with a mean and standard deviation. The existing 1000-repetition coverage/power experiments and interval-reporting practices are retained. The 50 runs concern the new check, not an increase in repetitions of earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the CelebA comparison retain their values. Added results include SLQ mean 16189.15 versus exact 16177.51, with standard deviation 57.13; coverage declining from 0.906 to 0.462 as encoder perturbation increases from 0 to 0.05; and WikiText-2 interval curves in Figure 24.

T1.justification: Adds SLQ trace reasoning and formal m-dependence conditions C1–C2 in D.3. Most Edgeworth theory is relocated, but Corollary B.1 now equates coverage probabilities that v3 Corollary 4.1 only stated converge to the same level. The new stochastic trace formula also omits 1/m averaging as printed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims: unbiased relative-KL estimation at the parametric rate, conditional comparison, Edgeworth refinement for small samples, and statistically confident comparisons consistent with benchmark findings.

C2.justification: Adds specific qualifications about sampling uncertainty, safety being outside relative-KL significance, CLT versus Edgeworth selection, and image-computation costs. It interprets the new approximation checks and argues for applicability to dependent WikiText data, without specifying dependence-adjusted variance estimation.

D1.justification: Adds a reproduction-code link, explicit disclosure of exact autograd Jacobian computation, SLQ implementation settings, and TriviaQA scoring of one reference answer without normalization or aggregation over acceptable answers. General parallelization and pre-storage suggestions from v3 are removed.

R1.justification: Adds Hutchinson (1989) and Ubaru, Chen and Saad (2017) for stochastic trace estimation and SLQ, while removing the Grathwohl et al. FFJORD citation. Related work also adds the computational cost of refitting as a distinction from likelihood-ratio comparisons.

P1.justification: Includes localized editing, numeric citations replacing author–year citations, relocation of studentized Edgeworth theory to Appendix B, reorganization of experimental details in D, and movement of future directions to Appendix E. Most prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a normal-input excerpt, with its full earlier content retained as Figure 22. Histograms move from Figure 4 to Figure 23, and a redundant main-text multilayer-sigmoid display is removed while appendix results remain. Table 4 and Figure 24 are added, with corresponding layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity evidence, SLQ check, code link and explicit TriviaQA scoring details improve transparency while retaining earlier benchmark results. However, the new SLQ formula lacks probe averaging, and the dependent-data validity argument supplies no dependence-adjusted variance estimator. These unresolved issues concern the correctness of the added extensions, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
